samples.summary: `dropStaleStyleOff` loops `store.applyStyle`, splitting one `setBlockType` user action into N+1 undo units
samples.evidence: `dropStaleStyleOff` (document.ts:474-501) issues one `this.store.applyStyle(...)` per inline run (line 497-499), and `setBlockType` (line 539-545) already issued its own `store.setBlockType`. On `YorkieDocStore` each of these is a separate `this.doc.update()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1763) and therefore a separate undo unit — the store interface says so explicitly: "a loop of `applyStyle()` calls produces one undo unit per call on stores (like YorkieDocStore) whose undo granularity is tied to the write itself. Prefer [applyStyles]" (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:82-89). So converting a Heading 6 with 3 style-off runs to a paragraph needs 4 Cmd+Z presses, and the first press lands the document in a half-reverted state (paragraph again carrying `italic:false`). No undo-grouping wrapper exists anywhere in the repo (grep for undoGroup/beginUndo/withUndo returns nothing). `store.applyStyles` exists precisely for this and is not used.

samples.summary: `Doc.normalizeInlinesArray` still merges structural inlines — the exact image-loss case the new `normalizeInlines` guard was added for
samples.evidence: The change adds `!isStructuralInline(last) && !isStructuralInline(inline)` to `normalizeInlines` (block-helpers.ts:94-99) because merging two equal image runs "silently drops the second while the offsets keep counting both". The sibling copy in `Doc.normalizeInlinesArray` (document.ts:992-1009) still merges on `inlineStylesEqual` alone, and it is reached from the table cell-merge path (document.ts:890-893) which concatenates the inlines of blocks taken from the merged cells. Two identical adjacent images inside a cell block therefore still collapse into one 2-char run under a single `style.image` — one image lost, offsets still counting both.

samples.summary: `captureFormatAtCursor` ignores the hyperlink underline default it is supposed to bake in, so copying format from a link yields `underline: false`
samples.evidence: `on('underline')` reads `raw.underline ?? defaults.underline` (text-editor.ts:3012-3013), where `defaults` is only the *named-style* layer (`styleDefaultsAtCursor`). The change itself documents a second implicit default layer: on an `href` run absent `underline` means underlined (paint-layout.ts:398-401, and the new comment at paint-layout.ts:386-390). Copying the format of a link therefore produces a buffer with `href: <url>` (spread from `raw`) *and* `underline: false`, and painting it creates a link that is explicitly not underlined — the opposite of the "effective value" contract the new doc comment states.

samples.summary: Stale `false` overrides are only cleaned up on `setBlockType`; block merge/split and `removeLink` strand them identically
samples.evidence: `dropStaleStyleOff` is called only from `setBlockType` (document.ts:544). The same stranding happens on two other paths: (a) `mergeBlock` (document.ts:380) pulls a Heading-6 block's runs — which legitimately carry `italic: false` per `styleOffAsClear` — into a paragraph, where nothing under the run supplies italic any more; (b) `removeLink` writes `{ href: undefined }` (editor.ts:3020, text-box-editor.ts:1240) leaving the `underline: false` that `styleOffAsClear` kept only because of the href. Both leave the dead flag the change describes as the #749 hazard: the run can never re-merge (`inlineStylesEqual` compares strictly) and stays pinned against a later style redefinition.
searchedFor: grep dropStaleStyleOff (only definition + one call site)
grep setBlockType( across packages/docs and packages/frontend

samples.summary: `styleOffAsClear` silently degrades to "clear everything" when the block cannot be found
samples.evidence: When `findBlock(blockId)` returns undefined (line 444), `defaults` becomes `{}` (line 450) and the link guard is short-circuited by `block &&` (line 453). Every boolean `false` is then rewritten to `undefined`, including `underline: false` on a hyperlink run and an override of a named-style default — exactly the two cases the method exists to preserve, turning the toggle-off into a permanent visual no-op instead of failing loudly or leaving the patch untouched. A missing block should fall back to the conservative behaviour (return `style` unchanged), not the aggressive one.

samples.summary: `clipboard.mergeInlines` merges on style equality alone, without the new structural-inline exception
samples.evidence: `mergeInlines` (clipboard.ts:445-455) is the paste-path counterpart of `normalizeInlines` and still merges any two runs whose styles compare equal. `inlineStylesEqual` compares images by value, so two identical adjacent image (or pageNumber) inlines would be concatenated and one payload lost. I could not find an `img`/`￼` producer in the HTML walk that feeds it, so it may be unreachable today, but it is the one remaining copy of the merge rule that does not carry the invariant the diff establishes.

mergedFrom.summary: `styleOffAsClear` silently degrades to "clear everything" when the block cannot be found
mergedFrom.evidence: When `findBlock(blockId)` returns undefined (line 444), `defaults` becomes `{}` (line 450) and the link guard is short-circuited by `block &&` (line 453). Every boolean `false` is then rewritten to `undefined`, including `underline: false` on a hyperlink run and an override of a named-style default — exactly the two cases the method exists to preserve, turning the toggle-off into a permanent visual no-op instead of failing loudly or leaving the patch untouched. verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repo. `dropStaleStyleOff` (document.ts:474-501) materializes all edits into an array and then loops `store.applyStyle` once per run (497-499); `setBlockType` (document.ts:539-544) issues its own `store.setBlockType` first. On `YorkieDocStore`, `applyStyle` opens its own `this.doc.update()` per call (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1763) and `setBlockType` another (1461), so one user action becomes N+1 Yorkie undo units, with intermediate undo states leaving a paragraph still carrying stale `italic:false` runs. The store interface explicitly forbids this pattern and points at the fix (store.ts:82-89), and `applyStyles` exists and batches into a single `doc.update` while composing same-block cache edits correctly (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1786-1828) — it is directly usable with the already-collected `edits` array but is not used here. No undo-grouping wrapper exists in the docs store (store.ts has no batch/transaction API; the `batch()` I found is in the unrelated packages/notes store). Real, reachable on any Heading 6 -> paragraph conversion, and an incorrect-state-update / broken-invariant defect in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: `Doc.normalizeInlinesArray` still merges structural inlines — the exact image-loss case the new `normalizeInlines` guard was added for
finding.evidence: The change adds `!isStructuralInline(last) && !isStructuralInline(inline)` to `normalizeInlines` (block-helpers.ts:94-99) because merging two equal image runs "silently drops the second while the offsets keep counting both". The sibling copy in `Doc.normalizeInlinesArray` (document.ts:992-1009) still merges on `inlineStylesEqual` alone, and it is reached from the table cell-merge path (document.ts:890-893) which concatenates the inlines of blocks taken from the merged cells. Two identical adjacent images inside a cell block therefore still collapse into one 2-char run under a single `style.image` — one image lost, offsets still counting both.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. `normalizeInlines` (block-helpers.ts:89-104) and `TextEditor.normalizeInlineList` (text-editor.ts:3810-3827) both carry the new `!isStructuralInline(last) && !isStructuralInline(inline)` guard, but `Doc.normalizeInlinesArray` (document.ts:992-1009) merges on `inlineStylesEqual` alone and never references `isStructuralInline` (grep shows no use of it in document.ts). `inlineStylesEqual` compares images by value through `imageDataEqual` (types.ts:479-499), so two identical adjacent image inlines compare equal and get concatenated into one 2-char run under a single `style.image` — the exact loss mode documented at types.ts:501-515 ("the second is lost while the offsets still count both"). The path is live: `mergeCells` (document.ts:852-893) normalizes every block of the top-left cell at line 892, and images inside table cells are a rendered, supported case (table-renderer.ts:424-434). No guard elsewhere prevents a cell block from holding two adjacent identical images — the other two normalizers now deliberately preserve that shape. Silent image loss plus desynced offsets is a data-loss/broken-invariant bug in the correctness lane; no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Underline toggle-off on a hyperlink becomes a permanent no-op: the guard only knows about named-style defaults, but the painter's link default also keys on `underline === undefined`

verdict.reason: The finding claims `styleOffAsClear` consults only named-style defaults and therefore rewrites underline-off on a link run to `undefined`. The code is not as described: document.ts:453 contains an explicit second guard, `if (key === 'underline' && block && rangeCarriesLink(block, from, to)) continue;`, sitting directly after the named-style guard at 452. `rangeCarriesLink` (document.ts:55-64) detects any touched run with an `href`, including the collapsed-caret-on-boundary case, so the explicit `false` is retained and never converted to `undefined`. The reviewer's cited evidence location (document.ts:413) is a line of the doc comment, not the guard; that same comment (416-429) enumerates the hyperlink default as "layer 2" and states the whole-slice retention is deliberate. paint-layout.ts:397-400 does key the link underline on `style.underline === undefined`, but with the stored `false` retained, line 400 never fires, so the painter does not re-underline and the read side does not disagree with the paint. The companion `dropStaleStyleOff` carries the same exemption (document.ts:489), and both `Doc` write paths into `store.applyStyle` (399, 514) route through `styleOffAsClear`, so no call site reaches the write unguarded. The described defect does not exist in this repository.

finding.summary: Clearing a boolean key can make an image run byte-identical to an adjacent identical image run, and `normalizeInlines` (unlike the paste path) merges structural inlines — losing one image
finding.evidence: `normalizeInlines` (block-helpers.ts:76-86) merges any two adjacent runs for which `inlineStylesEqual` is true, with **no** `isStructuralInline` guard. `inlineStylesEqual` compares images through `imageDataEqual` (types.ts:383-398), i.e. two *identical* images (copy/paste an image beside itself) compare equal — exactly the case types.ts:432-436 and TextEditor.normalizeInlineList (view/text-editor.ts:3722, issue #726) say must never merge. Before this change a toggle-off wrote `bold: false` onto the styled image run, which differed from its unstyled twin and kept them split; now `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:399-418) rewrites it to `undefined` and `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325) *deletes* the key, so run A's style becomes exactly `{image}` — equal to twin B. `applyInlineStyle` ends with `normalizeInlines(newInlines)` (line 380), which concatenates them into one 2-character run under a single `style.image`: the second image is dropped from the model while the offsets still count both characters (layout emits one image segment for the 2-char inline). Repro: two adjacent identical images, image A bolded, B not; select only A and press Cmd+B (summary reads bold-on for that run, so the toggle sends `bold:false`).

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — that `normalizeInlines` merges adjacent equal-style runs "with no `isStructuralInline` guard" — is false in this repository. `packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:94-99` gates the merge on `last && !isStructuralInline(last) && !isStructuralInline(inline) && inlineStylesEqual(...)`, so two image runs never take the concatenating branch no matter what `inlineStylesEqual`/`imageDataEqual` (`packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:458-499`) report. `isStructuralInline` (`packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:513-515`) returns true for any inline with `style.image !== undefined` or `style.pageNumber === true`, which covers both twins in the repro. The docstring at `block-helpers.ts:80-87` states exactly this contract, and the reviewer's precise repro is an existing passing-style test: `applyInlineStyle(block, 0, 1, { bold: undefined })` over two identical image runs asserts two runs survive with both `style.image` intact (`packages/docs/test/store/block-helpers.test.ts:476-488`), with sibling cases for pasted identical images (`:464-474`) and page numbers (`:490-496`). The `styleOffAsClear`/`mergeInlineStyle` half of the story is real (run A's style does become `{image}`), but the data-loss step it is claimed to enable — `normalizeInlines` at `block-helpers.ts:474` concatenating the two image runs into one 2-char inline — cannot happen. No image is dropped, so there is no correctness defect on this path.

mergedFrom.summary: Every B/I/U/S toggle-off now emits a `removeStyleByPath` op instead of a `styleByPath` set; concurrent-edit resolution between remove-attribute and set-attribute ops is not the same LWW path the old `bold=false` write used

finding.summary: Every style write, including the now-hot pure-clear toggle-off, re-asserts the node's full existing attribute map, which can clobber a concurrent remote attribute change
finding.evidence: `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], { ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs })` re-sends every attribute already on the node even when `styleAttrs` is empty (the pure-clear case `{bold: undefined}` that, per the comment added at lines 1873-1875, is now every B/I/U/S toggle-off). The comment two lines above states styleByPath 'only merges', so passing `existingAttrs` is unnecessary; because it is sent with a fresh local timestamp, an LWW-per-attribute Tree resolves it over a concurrent peer's change to an unrelated attribute (e.g. peer sets `color` while this client toggles bold off), reverting the peer's edit. The delta puts this redundant full-attribute rewrite on the hottest editing path.

verdict.reason: The finding quotes `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], { ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs })`, but that code is not in the repository. At yorkie-doc-store.ts:1954 the call is `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], styleAttrs);` — only the patch's own serialized attributes. `existingAttrs` does not appear anywhere in packages/frontend/src/app/docs (grep returned no matches), and no `styleByPath` call site in the file spreads a node's current attribute map. The comment at lines 1944-1948 explicitly documents the opposite of the claim ("Only the patch's own attributes are sent. Re-asserting the node's existing attributes would … clobber a concurrent remote change"). Furthermore, the pure-clear toggle-off case the finding calls "hottest path" writes nothing at all: line 1953 guards with `if (Object.keys(styleAttrs).length > 0)`, and clearing is routed through `tree.removeStyleByPath(..., removeAttrs)` at line 1957, scoped to the named keys. There is no full-attribute rewrite and therefore no clobbering of a concurrent peer's unrelated attribute change on this path.

finding.summary: Yorkie tree write ignores the superscript/subscript mutual exclusion that the cache write applies, so the CRDT keeps both flags while the local cache shows one
finding.evidence: `applyStyle` (line 1707) updates the cache with `applyInlineStyleHelper(block, from, to, style)`, and that helper (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:337-343) resolves `{superscript:true}` into `{superscript:true, subscript:undefined}` and, via `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325), *deletes* `subscript` from the run. The tree path (`applyStyleInTree`, line 1716) is handed the RAW `style`: `serializeInlineStyle(style)` at line 1882 emits only `superscript:'true'` and `removedInlineStyleAttrs(style)` at line 1883 returns `[]` because `subscript` is not a key of the patch. Since `styleByPath` only merges, the pre-existing `subscript='true'` attribute survives on the Tree node. Ctrl+. on subscripted text (text-editor.ts:899) therefore leaves the CRDT with both `superscript` and `subscript` set; `parseInlineStyle` (line 168-173) reads both back on reload or on any remote-driven cache invalidation, so the run silently changes appearance/state relative to what the user saw. This is exactly the 'styleByPath cannot delete' class of bug the surrounding comment block (lines 1871-1881) claims is handled on this path.

verdict.reason: The described defect is not present. `applyStyleInTree` does not pass the raw patch to serialization: yorkie-doc-store.ts:1949 computes `const resolved = resolveScriptExclusion(normalizeStyleClears(style))` and lines 1950-1951 feed that `resolved` value (not `style`) to `serializeInlineStyle` and `removedInlineStyleAttrs`. `resolveScriptExclusion` (block-helpers.ts:410-420) sets `subscript = undefined` with the key present when `superscript` is truthy, and `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:155-163) detects exactly that shape (`key in style && style[key] === undefined`), so it returns `['subscript']` and line 1957 issues `tree.removeStyleByPath(...)` for each inline in the range. The CRDT therefore drops `subscript` in the same way `applyInlineStyleHelper`/`mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:437, 461, 396) drops it from the cache. The multi-range `applyStyles` path uses the same helper (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1813), so it is covered too. The finding's quoted line numbers and quoted mechanism do not match the repository.
